speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing difficulty conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity; to help me understand your situation better, have you noticed any specific pain locations, such as deep pelvic pain or pain at the entrance?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. You mentioned pelvic floor muscle tension; have you noticed any specific tenderness in that area when I press on it during a physical exam, and does the pain radiate to your lower back or thighs?

speaker: Patient
text: he is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history raises concern for provoked vestibulodyinia (vulvar vestibulitis) given the pain at the entrance and pelvic floor tension. Can you describe if the pain is sharp and localized to the opening, and has this occurred since your previous diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic floor muscle tone assessment; REQUEST IMAGES: Vulvar inspection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Provoked Vestibulodynia (Vulvar Vestibulitis) with associated Pelvic Floor Dysfunction.

The normal muscle tone assessment and lack of radiation to the back help rule out deep infiltrating endometriosis or significant myofascial trigger points beyond the vestibule. Given the localized pain at the entrance, the history of failed conception due to painful intercourse (dyspareunia), and the exclusion of other systemic causes, this confirms the diagnosis of provoked vestibulodynia. Treatment will focus on topical anesthetics, pelvic floor physical therapy, and behavioral counseling.
